subject: religious-studies
title: Soul, Body and the Person
welcome_lead: Are we souls with bodies, bodies with souls, or something more? Step into millennia of debate.
meta_desc: Religious Studies Adventure: religious and philosophical views of soul, body and person.
final_note: You have weighed dualism and materialism. The question of personhood remains alive today.

concepts.def: View that humans are composed of two distinct substances, body and soul (Descartes).
Aristotelian view, adapted by Aquinas, that the soul is the form of the body.
View that humans consist solely of physical matter, denying a non-physical soul.
In Hindu thought, the eternal self or soul, ultimately identical with Brahman.
Buddhist doctrine of no-self: there is no permanent, unchanging soul.
Christian and Islamic belief in the bodily resurrection of the dead.

walkthroughs.body_html: Plato treated the soul as immortal and trapped in the body; Aristotle viewed the soul as the form of the body, providing its life and intelligibility. Christian thinkers like Augustine drew on Platonism; Aquinas integrated Aristotelian hylomorphism with belief in personal immortality and bodily resurrection.

Hindu traditions affirm atman, the eternal self, whose true identity with Brahman is realised through spiritual discipline. The Buddha rejected such a permanent self with the doctrine of anatta; the apparent self is a stream of physical and mental aggregates (skandhas).

Modern science encourages physicalism; neuroscience locates mind in brain. Religious thinkers respond variously: some defend property dualism or emergence, others articulate non-reductive Christian materialism. Debates about personhood inform ethical questions on abortion, AI, end-of-life care and animal rights.

mcqs.q: What do Christians mean by resurrection, and how does it differ from reincarnation?
options: Resurrection is the once-for-all bodily raising to eternal life at the end of time (modelled on Christ's resurrection); reincarnation is the soul's repeated rebirth into new bodies. They are distinct doctrines from different religious traditions.
Do whatever your conscience tells you to do.
Christians believe everyone is reincarnated until they accept Jesus.
Resurrection and reincarnation are basically the same idea of life after death.

mcqs.q: What does Buddhism teach about suffering?
options: Christians believe everyone is reincarnated until they accept Jesus.
All existence involves dukkha (suffering/unsatisfactoriness), caused by tanha (craving and attachment); ending craving leads to liberation from suffering.
Buddhism teaches that suffering is caused by demons.
Buddhism teaches that life is nothing but pain and misery.
